PASSO 1: leia a palavra composta da dire: STEP 1: good news: you already read compounds like this in English: a "door key" is a key, a "key door" would be a door. German works the same way — the LAST part says what it is, the parts before say what kind. STEP 2: the difference: German writes it as ONE word («Haustürschlüssel», never «Haus Tür Schlüssel»), and the article comes from the last part.
PASSO 1: o alemão forma palavras NOVAS j: STEP 1: German builds NEW words by joining two or more: «Haus» + «Tür» → «Haustür» (front door). The first word tells you the TYPE, the last word says WHAT IT IS: «die Tür» is the base. STEP 2: the GENDER and the PLURAL of the compound come from the LAST word: «das Haus» + «die Tür» → «DIE Haustür» (feminine); «die Hand» + «das Tuch» → «DAS Handtuch» (towel). STEP 3: sometimes a LINKING ELEMENT appears: «-s», «-n», «-en», «-e»: «Wohnung-s-schlüssel», «Hunde-hütte». Rule of thumb: after words ending in «-ung», «-heit», «-keit», «-schaft», «-tion», use «-s». STEP 4: to READ a long compound, split it from BACK TO FRONT: «Haustürschlüssel» = the key (Schlüssel) to the door (Tür) of the house (Haus). STEP 5: compounds are written together, as one word — where English writes "front door key" as three words.
o português junta palavras com «de» («ch: English builds compounds too ("toothbrush", "front door key") — sometimes as one word, often as separate words. German always writes them as one word, and the gender is the gender of the last part.

PASSO 1: um PREFIXO muda o sentido de um: STEP 1: a PREFIX changes the meaning of a verb — like English under-stand, mis-take, re-turn. STEP 2: the INSEPARABLE prefixes are «BE-, ENT-, ER-, VER-, ZER-, GE-, MISS-»; they stay attached to the verb, are not stressed, and the Partizip II takes NO «ge-»: «verkaufen → verkauft», «besuchen → besucht». STEP 3: SEPARABLE prefixes include «AB-, AN-, AUF-, AUS-, EIN-, MIT-, NACH-, VOR-, ZU-, ZURÜCK-, WEG-»; they're stressed and the Partizip II has «ge-» in the middle: «einkaufen → eingekauft». STEP 4: useful meanings: «ver-» changes or goes wrong («verstehen» — understand, «verkaufen» — sell, «vergessen» — forget); «er-» result («erkennen» — recognize, «erreichen» — reach); «ent-» start or removal («entdecken» — discover, «entfernen» — remove); «zer-» destroy («zerstören», «zerbrechen» — break into pieces); «be-» direct object («besuchen» — visit, «bezahlen» — pay for). STEP 5: use logic to work it out: «kaufen» = buy, «verkaufen» = sell; «decken» = cover, «entdecken» = discover (dis-cover!).

PASSO 1: os SUFIXOS indicam o tipo de pa: STEP 1: SUFFIXES show the type of word and the gender. Many have English cousins. STEP 2: FEMININE nouns: «-UNG» (die Wohnung, die Meinung — often like English -ing), «-HEIT» and «-KEIT» (die Freiheit — freedom, die Kindheit — childhood, die Möglichkeit — possibility: like -hood, -dom, -ity), «-SCHAFT» (die Freundschaft — friendship: -ship!), «-TION» (die Information). STEP 3: nouns for PEOPLE: «-ER» (der Lehrer — teacher: -er!), «-IN» (die Lehrerin, the female form). STEP 4: DIMINUTIVES: «-CHEN» and «-LEIN» (always neuter): «das Mädchen», «das Büchlein». STEP 5: ADJECTIVES: «-LICH» (freundlich — friendly: -ly), «-IG» (ruhig — quiet: like -y), «-BAR» (lösbar — solvable: -able), «-LOS» (arbeitslos — jobless: -less!), «-VOLL» (sinnvoll — meaningful: -ful), «-ISCH» (typisch — typical: -ish/-ic), and the prefix «UN-» (negation, as in English): «unmöglich» (impossible). STEP 6: with these rules, you can guess the gender and meaning of new words.
